name: Tryout
why: Borrowing a shop member's On Recruit without taking it plays off the shop in few words; the choice of which effect is real every time.

name: Gather
why: Same three-round gain-plus-recruit-bonus template as Stash and Allowance; long text for a plain gain, nobody else at the table notices.

name: Walk-In
why: Blind recruit from the pile (red's allowed randomness) with a small gift to rivals; owner can't know what arrives, so the choice is thin.

name: Promote
why: Trading up into a rival's better member is red's best moment: aimed at a rival, feeds Foster Parents and Deprogrammers, a trailing player can grab the leader's engine.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote; giving away the pricier member is rarely right, so it mostly repeats its sibling with a weaker pull.

name: Initiation
why: A free 8-cost recruit in round III is a clear burst a trailing player can grab; little decision beyond which member.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Round Start same-cost swap with a rival aims well and feeds Foster Parents; fires once per round, the victim gets an equal-cost member back so it stings mildly.

name: Volunteer
why: Pure cheap filler: worth 1 follower and one red member for the contest; nothing to feel or decide.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two recruits for one, counts 3 toward the red-member contest; clear and strong, the choice is only when to afford 9.

name: Proselytizers
why: A simple trigger on what red already does most; fires 1-2 times a round, stacks with Recruit Twice and Mentor, but 8 total cost for +1s.

name: Mob
why: Up to +6 followers a round for the member leader; it is the contest twice over, so it only rewards whoever is already ahead in red members.

name: Recruiter
why: +1 red per recruit is close to a flat red gain; 6 cost for small refunds, autopilot.

name: Patriarch
why: Generic end-game per-member count; works the same in any cult and rewards the biggest cult.

name: Foster Parents
why: Plays off Promote, Demote, Body Snatchers, Poach, Double Agent and rival gifts; cheap, counts 2, and builds a member-trading engine in few words.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Turns red's member-taking into a follower sting; counts 4 for 3 cost is very cheap for the red contest, close to must-buy.

name: Panel
why: A Promote or Demote on recruit is a strong red link, but 'promote or demote' needs the space text looked up, and it's not clear whose members it reaches.

name: Loyalists
why: Blocks Body Snatchers, Promote, Demote and Anarchist swaps; unclear whether Poach or Kidnapper count as a swap, and it shuts off red's main answer.

name: Clerk
why: Flat +1 red a round for 5 cost: the forgettable one-color gainer, dead at its price.

name: Sleep In
why: Big gain for giving up tempo, and the Goes Last token aims straight at the went-last contest; everyone watches who holds it.

name: Hold Up
why: 'Even yours' makes the skip a real timing puzzle; a sting everyone can see coming, feeds Gossip and fights Early Birds.

name: Right Away
why: Two turns in a row in one line; feeds Courier and Hot Streak, small gain on its own.

name: Last Call
why: Pays for holding minions back and grabs the went-last contest; 'your other minions are placed after everyone else's' takes a second read.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row bends the snake in five words; a trailing player can grab a run of spaces.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in round III is a clear burst; generic rather than purple's turn-order idea.

name: Courier
why: +1 of every other color on each consecutive turn makes Right Away and Crunch Time explode; a visible engine with a big moment.

name: Night Watch
why: '+1 follower per minion on it' is unclear (on the token? on spaces?); passive payout off rivals' Sleep In and Last Call with no decision.

name: Night Owls
why: A free extra minion each round from II, placed last, helps the went-last contest; strong but 8 cost and wordy timing.

name: Early Birds
why: A clean counter to Hold Up and Bouncers in four words; does nothing on its own and switches off purple's skip answer.

name: Bouncers
why: Two rivals skip on recruit: a big, visible moment that feeds Gossip; a fair sting since it's once and shared.

name: Gossip
why: Rides on Hold Up and Bouncers, anyone's skips; fires maybe once a round, so 6 cost is a stretch.

name: Timekeeper
why: The per-member-of-my-color end-game count shared with Snobs and Old Money; no interaction, rewards the deep purple cult.

name: Closer
why: Pays the went-last plan already in purple's contest; +4 purple once a round if you pull it off.

name: Hot Streak
why: Once-per-game burst that pays off Crunch Time and Right Away; counting 'turns in a row just before this one' needs care at a table.

name: Picket Line
why: Passive +1 purple when rivals use purple; counts 3 for 4 cost is its real value, the ability is forgettable.

name: Bell Ringer
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do (when the Goes Last token was placed relative to a skip)
why: Stacked conditions about skips, consecutive turns and when the token was placed; nobody can say when it fires and the table must remember token timing.

name: Toast
why: A big silver gain whose gift to rivals matters because silver's contest is most silver held; a gift the table likes.

name: Polish
why: Clean silver-to-colors converter; useful fuel, little table reaction.

name: Party Gifts
why: Spend the bank's silver on rivals for 6 followers; aiming the gift at who's racing the silver contest is a real choice.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pick what to give you, then get silver; who chooses and what you'll get isn't known in advance, and rivals act on your turn.

name: Sweet Talk
why: +3 silver then convert freely; overlaps Polish and Smooth Talkers, already doable another way.

name: Largesse
why: Round III giveaway for up to 10 followers that also feeds rivals' silver contest; a burst a trailing player can use.

name: Godparent
why: Give away a member for its cost in followers; plays off Martyrs, Foster Parents and Old Maid, with real timing and target choices.

name: Hostesses
why: Automatic gift engine each round: +3 followers for 3 silver to rivals; no decision once bought.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver when silver is gifted; 'gifted' by whom is unclear and the payoff is forgettable.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Turns cheap members into +4 followers on each Silver space; giving a member is a real gift and a real choice, fires most rounds.

name: Toastmaster
why: Cheap filler: +1 follower per Silver space, plain and forgettable.

name: Debutantes
why: Double your silver once, with rivals topped up; timing it before a silver-contest count or Smooth Talkers spend is a real call.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as wild currency makes silver a real engine; 11 cost and overlaps Sweet Talk.

name: Philanthropist
why: A smaller one-shot Party Gifts; repeats a sibling space.

name: Creditor
why: Forced trade of 2 followers for 3 silver each round; aim it at the leader, but 'once per round' on a 4-follower swing is strong.

name: Debt Collectors
why: A once-per-game plain steal of up to 6 silver dressed as debt; clear, timing matters for the silver contest.

name: High Society
why: Passive +1 follower on rivals' Silver spaces; the same shape as Picket Line in another color.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (most silver a rival holds minus yours)
why: Catches you up to the richest silver rival each round; the condition compares rivals' resources and pays nothing when you lead.

name: Harvest
why: Yellow's plain fuel anchor: colors you choose feed full sets.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads the board for which color is crowded; a good table read, though the name and idea sit loosely in yellow.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards a new color of member, yellow's breadth idea; the three-round number ladder adds reading.

name: Housewarming
why: A free new-color recruit up to 5 is a strong, clear yellow moment that builds toward Big Tent.

name: Melting Pot
why: Pays for breadth of members in chosen colors; clear, moderate.

name: Makeover
why: Rearrange everything into full sets right before the count; a round III swing with a real timing call.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills the colors you lack each round, so it pays more to the player with gaps; clean set-building.

name: Duty Collector
why: Small passive gains when rivals recruit your colors; fires a few times a round, little to feel.

name: Tourist
why: Up to +8 followers a round for holding every color; a clear payoff for yellow's spread, 7 cost.

name: Seamstress
why: Once-per-game doubling of full sets is a big moment, but what 'double your full sets' gives you needs explaining.

name: Dyer
why: The Tourist shape paying yellow instead of followers; a weaker sibling.

name: Meddler
why: Changing each rival's resource can break their sets; 'one for one' and who picks need a second read.

name: Drifters
why: Choose its color: plays off Big Tent, Mob, the red contest and every per-color count; a clever cheap connector.

name: Big Tent
why: Up to +2 per color with one member sharpens yellow's breadth into a clear end-game plan.

name: Caravan
why: +1 of each held color every round fuels sets; strong but 9 cost and pays the already-wide player.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
why: Yellow as wild for full sets ties the color's resource straight to its contest in one line.

name: Savings
why: Blue gain plus an optional shop cycle before recruiting; two small effects.

name: Out of Style
why: Wipe a color out of the shop to deny rivals and gain blue; feeds Patroness and Scavenger.

name: Peek
why: Set up the pile and recruit from it; big blue gain, but stacking the next four is a lot to hold.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two recruits for the most-members contest, in two words.

name: Bury
why: Shop cycling for half-cost blue; repeats Savings and Out of Style more weakly.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in round III: a burst any trailing player can grab.

name: Hawker
why: An auction-like offer around the table that pays you either way; who pays what and in which order takes explaining, and rivals choose on your turn.

name: Patroness
why: Pays off Out of Style, Window Dressers and Trendsetters; unclear if it's +1 per member or per event.

name: Snobs
why: End-game per-blue-member count, the same shape as Timekeeper and Old Money.

name: Window Shopper
why: Clears two shop members each round for their colors; reshapes rivals' shop, feeds Patroness.

name: Shopaholics
why: Recruit twice every turn: a huge engine for the member leader that's hard to answer at 9 cost.

name: Window Dressers
why: A one-time shop flush; its counts-3 for 4 cost is the real draw.

name: Doormen
why: Once a round you swap a rival's member for a shop member of your choice; strong and aimed, but two clauses and a cost rule for one idea.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue when buying followers has nothing to do with blue's recruiting; forgettable.

name: Trendsetters
why: A shop cycle per recruit; repeats Window Dressers, value is mostly counts 3 for 4.

name: Critic
why: +1 follower when rivals recruit blue; cheap and quiet.

name: Scavenger
hardFail: turn flow: asks its owner to choose and recruit during a rival's turn
why: Grabbing what rivals bury is clever play off Out of Style, Bury and Window Shopper, but the owner decides and recruits during another player's turn.

name: Help Yourself
why: The color's plain steal, scaling by round and aimed as you choose; fires every time.

name: Stash
why: The Gather and Allowance template again; nothing magenta about it.

name: Lie Low
why: A shield against steals for the round; 'this round' needs a marker on the table.

name: Heist
why: Steal 3 followers is a 6-point swing aimed at the leader; clear and a catch-up tool.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim chooses their own punishment, a member or its cost; it feels bad, and the rival chooses on your turn.

name: Poach
why: Taking any rival's member free in round III is a big aimed burst and the answer to a runaway engine.

name: Cutpurse
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (the rival with the most resources)
why: Steals 1 from the richest rival each round; small and automatic.

name: Accomplice
why: Cheap one-time steal of 3, clean filler for magenta.

name: Grifter
why: Steal 1 per 2 members rewards buying it late into a wide cult; a timing call with a big payoff.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A 2-steal right before contests are scored can flip any contest; rivals plan around it every round.

name: Desperado
why: Steals grow while you trail in followers, which also fits White's fewest-followers contest; built-in catch-up.

name: Extortionist
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (the rival with the most resources)
why: A bigger Cutpurse, repeating its sibling with the same rival-resource target.

name: Bodyguards
why: Shuts off every steal against its owner; protects the leader and turns off magenta's whole answer.

name: Double Agent
why: Plant yourself in a rival's cult and take their member; plays off Foster Parents and Deprogrammers, the rival gets a cheap member back.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a member from the biggest cult every round with no choice; losing members before round III feels robbed.

name: Shoplifter
why: +1 steal per recruit, automatic and small.

name: Fence
why: Being stolen from pays you; a counter that makes thieves think twice.

name: Allowance
why: The shared gain-plus-recruit-follower template; nothing white about it.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for paying big on a recruit; 'every 1 in round II' leaves round III unclear, and it fits white loosely.

name: Exchange
why: Resources to followers at 2 each; close to the follower buy, already doable another way.

name: Farewell
why: Cast out a member for its cost in followers is White's clearest idea; plays off Martyrs, the blue member contest and the shop.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell for white instead, set up for Cash In; a sibling repeat.

name: Cash In
why: The payoff of white's hoard in one line; Heiresses, Hoarder and Estate Sale all point here.

name: Recluse
why: Pays for staying small, matching white's 'not members' idea; a clear catch-up for small cults.

name: Landlord
why: Flat +2 white on recruit and each Round Start: the worst kind of one-color gainer.

name: Heiresses
why: White per member, then Cash In: a strong combo with a real once-per-game timing call.

name: Brokers
why: +1 per White action that gives followers stacks with Farewell, Exchange and Cash In; 'White action' needs a lookup.

name: Misers
why: Hold white for the end versus Cash In now; a real fork in white's plan.

name: Raiders
why: A one-time 4-follower steal; in a fewest-followers color it oddly helps the rival you rob win white's contest.

name: Cashier
why: A portable Cash In for 3 that plays off Heiresses and Hoarder; repeats its round III space.

name: Money Changers
why: Passive white off follower buys; quiet.

name: Martyrs
why: Leaving pays its cost: plays off Farewell, Godparent, Promote and Poach, and turns rivals' takes into gifts.

name: Old Money
why: The per-member-of-my-color end-game count again.

name: Hoarder
why: Turn everything white once, then Cash In; a clear setup at 8 cost.

name: Build Up
why: Green's plain fuel anchor.

name: Echo
why: Copy the previous action: plays off whatever the last player did, every turn a fresh read of the board.

name: Reprise
why: Copy one of your own spaces again; simple and good with your best minion.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival's On Recruit; the table watches what you take.

name: Cover
why: Use an empty space without blocking it; a clever twist on placement.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Replay every On Recruit you own in round III; pays off the whole cult.

name: Song Request
why: Copy a rival's space once a round, without placing a minion; strong reading of the board at 7 cost.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrow a rival's ability each round; strong, but the table must keep track of which ability it holds.

name: Impressionist
why: +1 of a color whenever anyone copies; quiet.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubles resources from copies, a green engine; 10 cost.

name: Fan Club
why: Copy the follower leader's space; a catch-up idea with no follower-buy condition on resources.

name: Roadie
why: Green per green member, the Dyer shape again.

name: Stunt Double
why: Repeat the action you just took on recruit; good after Spree or Housewarming.

name: Tribute Band
why: Do all of a rival's spaces once: a huge copy at 14 cost.

name: Doppelganger
why: Becomes a copy of your best member; unclear whether it copies counts-as and worth.

name: Agents
why: Blocks copies of your spaces; unclear what 'your actions' covers, and it's a counter only.

name: Encore
why: Doubles one On Recruit; a timing call that grows with what you buy next.

name: Party Crasher
why: Once, take a space a rival already holds; answers blocking.

name: Alchemists
why: Any resource pays any color when recruiting; strong at 5, counts 3.

name: Extra Hand
why: An extra minion once, at 9 cost.

name: Line Cutters
why: First every round and counts 3 for 2 cost: must-buy, and it steps on purple's turn-order idea.

name: Old Maid
why: A hot potato: worth giving away through Godparent, Double Agent, Promote and Demote; fits White's fewest-followers contest.

name: Dabblers
why: Two wild members for counts; 'wild' needs a rules lookup.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members within 2 cost once a round; strong, aimed, and the table watches.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancel a contest you don't lead; a clean anti-leader tool.

name: Con Men
why: Steal 5 on recruit; magenta's job with no color.

name: Sore Loser
why: Steal 5 followers from the round's top contest winner if you won none; built-in catch-up.
